samples.summary: The rewritten cell-text paint path (per-span segmentation, link color, per-span underline, and the recording of hit boxes during render) has no test at all — only the two leaf helpers are driven directly
samples.evidence: The diff rewrites `renderCellText`'s inner loop: it now calls `detectLinks` per line, splits the line into segments, paints link segments in `linkColor`, draws per-span underlines only when `!style?.u`, and calls `recordRenderedLink` for each span. Nothing exercises this. `packages/sheets/test/view/gridcanvas-links.test.ts` calls `GridCanvas.prototype.recordRenderedLink` and `linkAt` on a hand-built `this` (lines 30-60) and never reaches `renderCellText`; `packages/sheets/test/view/gridcanvas.test.ts` covers only `computeCheckboxBox`, `buildRenderableRefs` and `renderCellCheckbox`. So if `renderCellText` stopped calling `detectLinks`/`recordRenderedLink`, computed the wrong `lineStartX`, double-painted glyphs, or drew two underlines, every suite stays green — yet hover, cursor and click all read that map, so the whole feature would silently not work. The repo already has precedent for testing a paint helper with a mock ctx (`renderCellCheckbox` + `makeMockCtx`, gridcanvas.test.ts:104-213), so this was reachable.

samples.summary: The deliberate behavior change "formula cells are linkified too" (removal of the `cell?.f` guard) has no test
samples.evidence: `const linkUrl = cell?.f ? null : cellHyperlink(rawData)` is replaced by unconditional `lines.map(detectLinks)`, and the task doc records this as an explicit decision (docs/tasks/active/20260917-sheets-cell-link-spans-todo.md:65). No test covers it: cell-links.test.ts tests the pure detector (which never sees a cell), and no test drives `renderCellText` with a formula cell. Nothing would catch the guard being reintroduced, or a HYPERLINK() label being mis-linkified.
searchedFor: Grep for cell?.f / linkSpans / formula in sheets view tests

samples.summary: The linearity assertion is effectively vacuous for four of its five shapes because of the 2 ms floor
samples.evidence: `expect(large).toBeLessThan(Math.max(small, 2) * 8)` means that whenever the small measurement is sub-millisecond — which it is for a single-`@` 8 kB string, the scheme-lookalike run, and the at-sign run, since each is a bounded linear walk — the bound collapses to a fixed 16 ms rather than a growth ratio. A quadratic regression on those shapes at 32 kB would still measure well under 16 ms and pass. Only the `'https://['.repeat(n)` shape is expensive enough for the ratio to bite (the task doc's own mutation check reports 388 ms vs a 216 ms bound there). The suite therefore advertises linearity for five shapes while actually guarding one.

`linksInCell` filters by `sref` and de-duplicates by `url` (the fix for duplicate React keys / repeated URLs, per the task doc). gridcanvas-links.test.ts tests only `recordRenderedLink` and `linkAt`; worksheet-links.test.ts replaces `linksInCell` with a stub (`linksInCell: (sref) => cells[sref] ?? []`, worksheet-links.test.ts:~60), so the real implementation — including the dedup and the sref filter — is mocked away in the only place it is called. A regression would resurface duplicate keys in the card.

Nothing exercises this. `packages/sheets/test/view/gridcanvas-links.test.ts` calls `GridCanvas.prototype.recordRenderedLink` and `linkAt` on a hand-built `this` (lines 30-60) and never reaches `renderCellText`; `packages/sheets/test/view/gridcanvas.test.ts` covers only `computeCheckboxBox`, `buildRenderableRefs` and `renderCellCheckbox`. verdict.reason: The paint path described exists (the method is `renderCellContent`, not `renderCellText`): gridcanvas.ts:1696 calls detectLinks per line, :1800-1835 segments the line, paints link spans in linkColor, draws a per-span underline only when `!style?.u` (:1823-1831), and calls `this.recordRenderedLink` per span (:1833). No test anywhere in the repo exercises it. Grep for `renderCellContent` across all files matches only gridcanvas.ts and docs; the only test files importing gridcanvas are gridcanvas.test.ts (computeCheckboxBox/buildRenderableRefs/renderCellCheckbox) and gridcanvas-links.test.ts (recordRenderedLink/linkAt on a hand-built `this`). The `src/view/__tests__/cell-links.test.ts` suite the reviewer's glob missed covers only the pure helpers detectLinks/layoutLinkBoxes/clipLinkBox; worksheet-links.test.ts drives hover/click over fabricated RenderedLink objects. `toLineStartX` (layout.ts:68) has no test either, and there is no e2e/visual lane. So a painter that stopped calling recordRenderedLink, mis-computed lineStartX, double-painted glyphs or stacked underlines would leave every suite green while hover/cursor/click silently break — a user-visible feature failure with no meaningful coverage. No counterexample found.

finding.summary: The hover state machine (`updateLinkHover`/`resetLinkHover`) has no test at all
finding.evidence: `updateLinkHover` is the core of this feature: it debounces via `LinkHoverDelayMS`, falls back to the cell under the pointer when no span is hit (so crossing plain text between two links does not strobe), compares by URL list so a collaborator edit refreshes the card, and must emit `null` before opening a new card when moving link-cell → link-cell. None of this is exercised. `packages/sheets/test/view/worksheet-mouse.test.ts` only adds `resetLinkHover: vi.fn()` to two hand-built contexts and asserts the mock was called — the real `resetLinkHover`/`updateLinkHover` bodies (timer clearing, callback with `null`, dedup) are never executed. A regression here ships a card stuck over the wrong cell or a strobing popover with a green suite.

verdict.reason: A dedicated suite, packages/sheets/test/view/worksheet-links.test.ts, tests the hover state machine against the real prototype methods (it installs Worksheet.prototype.updateLinkHover/resetLinkHover/clearLinkHoverTimer/linkAtMouse/isInsideGrid onto a hand-built `this` at lines 65-69; only the emission callback is a vi.fn spy). Every behavior the finding says is unexercised has a test with fake timers: the 300ms LinkHoverDelayMS debounce (lines 81-99, asserting nothing at 299ms and emission at 300ms), the no-hit cell fallback that keeps the card open across plain text between two spans (lines 101-117), the synchronous null emission before opening a new card on link-cell -> link-cell (lines 119-138, toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith(null)), the URL-list comparison so a collaborator edit refreshes the card (lines 140-161), dedup while staying on the same links (163-175), header/outside-grid guard (177-186), and resetLinkHover's timer cancellation plus null callback and no-op-when-nothing-open (188-226). These map onto worksheet.ts:957-1031. The reviewer's observation about worksheet-mouse.test.ts mocking resetLinkHover is true but concerns a different suite; the state machine's own suite was not among the paths the reviewer searched.

finding.summary: The changed link-opening click path (read-only plain click, `e.detail === 1`, modifier for editors) is untested, and the only test that covered the old behavior was deleted
finding.evidence: `handleMouseDown` now opens a URL on a *plain* left click when `this.readOnly`, keeps Ctrl/Cmd for editors, and guards double-clicks with `e.detail === 1`. No test drives this: `grep -n mousedown packages/sheets/test` matches only `worksheet-list-popover.test.ts`, and `worksheet-readonly-editing.test.ts` covers only formula-bar/cell-input commits. Meanwhile the diff deletes `packages/sheets/src/view/__tests__/url-detect.test.ts`, which was the only coverage of the previous open-on-click detection (including its unsafe-protocol rejection at the click site). So a regression that makes an editor's ordinary click navigate away, or that opens two tabs on double-click, would pass CI.

verdict.reason: The changed click path IS tested. packages/sheets/test/view/worksheet-links.test.ts:298-382 ("handleMouseDown link opening") calls the real Worksheet.prototype.handleMouseDown with the real linkAtMouse/isInsideGrid and a stubbed window.open, asserting: plain click opens only when readOnly && openLinksOnClick (309-322); read-only without opt-in does not open (324-329); an editor's plain click does not open (331-334) — the exact "editor click navigates away" regression; ctrl/meta+click opens for editors (336-346); the e.detail===1 guard yields exactly one open across a detail:1 + detail:2 pair (348-354) — the "two tabs on double-click" regression; plus right-click, no-span and header-strip negatives (356-381). These assert the real side effect (window.open url/_blank/noopener,noreferrer) and non-invocation, so flipping the condition at worksheet.ts:3694-3707 fails them. The file is collected by vitest (packages/sheets/vite.config.ts sets only coverage options, so the default test include applies).

finding.summary: New frontend popover component ships with no test, including its `isSafeUrl` href guard
finding.evidence: `SheetLinkPopover` filters `urls` through `isSafeUrl` before putting each string into an `href`, truncates via `toLabel`, and swallows clipboard rejections so the check mark is not shown on failure. There is no `SheetLinkPopover.test.tsx` anywhere (glob `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/**/*.test.*` returns only CommentPopover, csv, image tests), even though the sibling `components/comments/CommentPopover.test.tsx` shows the harness exists. The href allowlist is a guard; if it were dropped or inverted nothing would fail. `toLabel`'s truncation branch (`tail.length > 40`) and the copy-failure branch are likewise unexercised.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test exists for SheetLinkPopover, but packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/components/SheetLinkPopover.test.tsx is present in the working tree and covers exactly the three behaviors named as unexercised. The isSafeUrl href guard is asserted at test:55-68 (it.each over javascript:, data:, blob:, file:///, and a malformed string, expecting an empty DOM and no link role) and test:70-80 (mixed safe/unsafe input yields exactly one link with the safe href) — dropping or inverting the filter at SheetLinkPopover.tsx:58 would fail these. toLabel's truncation branch (SheetLinkPopover.tsx:28, tail.length > 40) is exercised at test:94-104 with a 200-char path, asserting host-prefixed, length < 60, trailing ellipsis, and full URL retained in title; the mailto:/www. branches at test:82-92. The clipboard rejection branch (SheetLinkPopover.tsx:93-96) is covered at test:118-132, which stubs writeText to reject and asserts the sheet-link-copied check mark is absent, paired with the success case at test:106-116. The component is rendered for real with no vi.mock of @wafflebase/core/url, so it is not over-mocked. The test is actually executed: vite.config.ts:373-383 includes src/**/*.test.tsx under jsdom with setupFiles tests/setup.ts, and tests/setup.ts:3 loads @testing-library/jest-dom/vitest providing the matchers used. The reviewer's own cited glob returns this file.
